record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.context_brief: wild attractors for real Hénon maps
record.original_question: Does there exist a real Hénon map, possibly of higher degree, that has a wild attractor: a Cantor set that attracts a set of positive Lebesgue measure but is strictly contained in a transitive set?

evidence.quote: Question 1. — Can we find a Hénon map (of some degree) which admits a wild attractor, i.e., a Cantor set which attracts a set of Lebesgue positive measure and which is strictly included in a transitive set ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real Hénon-type map is a polynomial diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^2$ of the form $H(x,y) = (p(x) - by,\, x)$, where $p:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a real polynomial of degree $d\ge 2$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$. A compact invariant set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ for $H$ is called an attractor for a set of positive Lebesgue measure if its basin $\{z\in\mathbb{R}^2 : \omega(z)\subset A\}$ has positive (two-dimensional) Lebesgue measure. The set $A$ is said to be transitive if $H|_A$ has a dense orbit. A wild attractor for $H$ is a Cantor set $K \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (i.e., a non-empty compact, perfect, totally disconnected $H$-invariant set) such that:
(i) $K$ attracts a set of positive Lebesgue measure in $\mathbb{R}^2$;
(ii) there exists a transitive $H$-invariant compact set $T$ with $K \subsetneq T$.

Question: Does there exist a real polynomial Hénon-type map $H$ (of some degree $d\ge 2$) that admits a wild attractor in the sense above?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open question in a recent list of open problems on Hénon maps. While wild attractors are known to exist for one-dimensional unimodal maps (Bruin–Keller–Nowicki–van Strien), no analog for real Hénon maps has been constructed; the question appears still open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Wild Sets with Collet-Eckmann Points and Infinitely Many Sinks
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on wild sets in higher-dimensional dynamics, no construction of a wild attractor for Hénon maps reported.
status_evidence.claim: No constructed example of a wild attractor for Hénon maps appears in subsequent literature.
